newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two more groups of Mexican "slaves" found in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Two more groups of Mexican "slaves" found in U.S.

text.p: Mexico said on Thursday that two more groups of deaf mute Mexicans had been discovered peddling trinkets for slave wages in the United States.

Mexicans were shocked by the discovery this week that about 60 of their deaf mute compatriots had been forced into virtual servitude in New York, held captive and made to sell keyrings and toys for a pittance in the subways and streets.
On Thursday Mexico's foreign ministry said another 24 deaf mute Mexicans had been found in a similar situation, selling keychains in the streets and squares of Sanford, North Carolina.
"(Mexico's Detroit consulate) took a declaration from one of them, who gave details of exploitation and abuse to which they had been subjected," the foreign ministry said.
Six others were found in Chicago.

The ministry did not say how the two groups had been discovered. But it said Mexico's consulates in New York, Chicago and Detroit, as well as the consular section of its Washington embassy, were striving to find and protect those affected.
Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo, on a visit to Chicago this week, denounced the abuses as "atrocities" and promised every help to the victims.
Their plight came to light on Saturday when four deaf mute Mexicans walked into a New York police station and, via notes and gestures, told a harrowing tale of exploitation and abuse.
Officials rescued 62 people from two cramped city apartments over the weekend. They said they were smuggled from Mexico over the California border and transported to Los Angeles and New York.
Seven people have been arrested, including four members of one family, in connection with the bizarre case. But officials are still seeking the alleged ringleader, identified as Reinaldo Paoletti.

The New York group was in the custody of city authorities and the American Red Cross was providing them with housing and food. U.S. authorities said earlier on Thuesday they would be allowed to stay in the United States while investigations are carried out.
Officials believe the ringleaders recruited their victims from homes and schools for the deaf and mute in Mexico, and promised them a better life in the United States.
